clue.text: Basic outline of plot on earth

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece sitting on another follows it, so the plot word comes after the earth word

parts.note: earth means ground, the soil underfoot
a plot is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A rough sketch of a burial plot in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect's first drawing of a building's layout at floor level is its basic outline.

explanation.surface: An exclamation urging someone to slash their wastefulness.
explanation.walkthrough: GASH is British slang for rubbish or spare material, especially in naval use.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a deep wound or slash; as slang it also names refuse or surplus stuff.

explanation.surface: A notable discrepancy turning up in an account's balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It makes no odds' means it makes no difference; 'the odds are in our favour' means the balance of advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds can mean a material difference, as in 'what's the odds?', and the balance of probability or advantage.

clue.text: Wild lions play finally in inquisitive way

indicators.note: wild suggests something unruly and disordered, so these letters are scrambled
finally points to the closing letter of the word play

explanation.surface: Untamed big cats romping at the end of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a prying, curious manner is acting with a busybody's curiosity.

clue.text: Fourth or fifth, perhaps, for the ideal break

parts.note: ideal means flawless, without fault
a break in a play or concert is an interval

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fourth or fifth day off would make the best holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: In music, the fourth, fifth and octave are termed perfect intervals; 'perhaps' marks these as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: In music theory the fourth and fifth are examples of this class of consonant pitch gap.

parts.note: cloakroom is a British euphemism for a lavatory, and the gents is the men's lavatory

explanation.surface: Wondering what elements might be found in a coat-check room.
explanation.walkthrough: GENTS is British for a men's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a commercial agent who buys and sells on another's behalf.

clue.text: Cold, centre part of freshwater fish

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a hub is the central part of a wheel or activity

explanation.surface: A chilled middle portion of a river fish served up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thick-bodied river species of the carp family, popular with anglers.

clue.text: Not as Irish constituents reveal chroniclers

indicators.note: constituents suggests the letters are the component parts, to be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Writers of records reveal people who are not Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers who record and study past events are chroniclers of history.

clue.text: His investigation into cells show what is the matter

definitions.text: His investigation into cells show what is the matter

parts.words: His investigation into cells show what is the matter
parts.note: reads like a prison or police inquiry, but cells are living cells and 'matter' is the chemical substance of life

explanation.surface: A man's search of prison cells reveals what is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist studying the chemistry of living cells reveals what organic material is made of.

clue.text: Minor way one can cut up?

definitions.text: Minor way one can cut up?

parts.words: Minor way one can cut up?
parts.note: a lesser road, and one a driver can cut up as a shortcut rather than carving it up

explanation.surface: A small route which someone might dissect.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor road branching off a main thoroughfare, handy for a shortcut.

indicators.note: change signals the remaining letters are rearranged
mainly means most of the word loose, dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: A capital city made mostly from loose coins.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Pin notices all over the place in this check?

indicators.note: all over the place suggests scattered disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Posting notices everywhere as part of an audit.
explanation.definitionFit: A close examination or audit is a check.

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, and AB is an able-bodied seaman
compound and solution both mean a mixture of substances

explanation.surface: Releasing a sailor's chemical mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text reads 'car', an OCR slip for 'tar', the sailor who gives AB. Discharge here is release from guilt, not a firing.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal release from sin or obligation is a kind of discharge.

clue.text: Province with a pound rate of exchange

parts.note: LB is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

indicators.note: exchange means swapping places, so the letters of rate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A region where a sterling exchange rate applies.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Canadian province, capital Edmonton.

parts.note: AD, anno domini, is the present era
verse means poetry

explanation.surface: A complaint that modern poetry is hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile or opposing circumstances are unfavourable and antagonistic.

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
able means skilled, expert

explanation.surface: A good-natured specialist driving along a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; in crosswords it is written with the letter I for the digit.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured and agreeable people are friendly.

parts.note: refers to Charles Pooter of 'The Diary of a ...' by George and Weedon Grossmith, an insignificant man

explanation.surface: A trivial writer of journals created by the Grossmith brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grossmiths' 1892 comic novel is the diary of a suburban clerk, a self-important but insignificant man.
explanation.definitionFit: An insignificant, unimportant person is a lightweight; the Grossmiths' clerk is the title figure of their diary.

explanation.surface: A tidy apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth means running without hitch, so orderly, and also even and level.

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters are put into an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: Remarking that it is rare for families to back such skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilled, businesslike conduct expected of an expert is competence.

explanation.surface: A timetable for a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a line of action, as a policy; it is also a planned series of lessons or treatments.

parts.note: to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: An elderly Englishman still charming.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract or captivate someone's interest is to charm them.

parts.note: links are seaside golf courses

explanation.surface: Someone creeping around golf courses in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipping along stealthily is moving furtively.

clue.text: Wooden idol broken in support of saint

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits beneath, so the idol letters come below the saint
broken signals the letters of idol are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A carved figure smashed while propping up a saint's statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive and unexpressive, like a wooden manner.

parts.note: looks like asking whether someone knows the language, but means the French word for an understanding between nations

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone can follow the French language.
explanation.walkthrough: The Entente Cordiale of 1904 was a friendly agreement between Britain and France.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for an agreement or friendly understanding between states.

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music to mean repeat

explanation.surface: Someone saying they got the bird two times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the bird' sounds like being booed off stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred wading bird of ancient Egypt with a long curved bill.

explanation.surface: A dejected county.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low is feeling depressed; Down is also a county of Northern Ireland.

indicators.note: buried in means the letters lie concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Skeletal remains interred in the sand of Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin plural for skeletal bones, used in anatomy.

indicators.note: paid out suggests money disbursed and spread around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge total being paid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wonderful or astonishing is sensational.

annotationWithheld.why: 'Number of children in England?' (4) for NINE: no sound parse found; the wordplay for NINE from 'of children in England' is unclear and the clue may be garbled

explanation.surface: An eye-catching beauty described as a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: Belladonna drops dilate the pupils, so literally open the eye; the name is Italian for beautiful lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade's extract widens pupils, once used cosmetically; in Italian the name means a fair woman.
